cards.note: Found in a photograph, not in the field: identified from an iNaturalist post more than a year after it was taken. Found first, published fourth — the observation predates every other recent record of the species by two years or more, which is why the paper reads as a locality record rather than a rediscovery.

cards.title: Scientists rediscover endangered Andean toad in Ecuador
cards.desc: The Tandayapa Andean toad was described in 1970 from a single individual found in Pichincha Province, Ecuador, and nothing was seen of it again. Forty-two years later a team refound it at Río Manduriacu — the reserve that is now its only known habitat, and whe
cards.citation: Reported in Amphibian & Reptile Conservation. Mongabay, 30 January 2015.
cards.note: Described as Andinophryne olallai; the genus was later folded into Rhaebo, so the same animal appears under both names.
